title: Hawkins, Stump Evans and Jimmy Dorsey on record
summary: Phillips explains Hawkins was heard only in big-band solos while Trumbauer's small-group records showed more; Lester listened to Prince Robinson and not much to Dorsey.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: What about the Hawkins things that were on those Fletcher Henderson records? He was doing some things, wasn't he?

Hawkins didn't have too much out. See, the thing about Hawkins and them, Hawkins and them didn't play too much...only with the band. But see, Frankie and them made records with the small groups, where you could really dig 'em. See, you'd dig a cat when he's out there playing in the small group more than you can... That's why people dug Louis. You didn't have to hear Louis play 16 bars or 18 bars, or maybe a chorus in a band... That ain't like you're out there playing by yourself; I mean, playing the whole record. You played four or five choruses or something like that.
What about Stump Evans?
Yeah...
Did Lester ever listen to Stump Evans or Prince Robinson?
Yeah, he listened to Prince.
On records?
Stump played alto, though.
Did he ever listen to Prince Robinson?
Yeah. The Cotton-Pickers was going pretty good in them days.
Any comments that he made about these people -- what he did like and what didn't like?
Phillips - 56
Mmm...
As you said, he didn't go for Freeman and he did go for Trumbauer.
Yeah, that was his main man, Trumbauer.
How about Jimmy Dorsey? Did he ever listen to Jimmy Dorsey?

Not too much. Because Jimmy Dorsey wasn't doing too much soloing either. You know, in his band... I think he was playing with Ben Pollack's band. He was back there in them times, '26... Because I heard him...
Yeah. He worked with Jean Goldkette and Whiteman, Vincent Lopez, Red Nichols, people like that. At least, that's according to John Chilton's book.
I think he and Benny Goodman all was with Ben Pollack at the same time.
I'm not sure that Jimmy Dorsey joined Pollack.
Benny was with him.
Yeah, Benny Goodman was with him.

See, at that time they used to make them records with five pieces and six pieces. See, you can dig a cat soloing moreso in a band, if he plays maybe 8 bars, or sometimes 16, or maybe one chorus. Never over a chorus they played in them big bands.
So that's the reason you didn't hear a lot of Hawkins, because he...
Phillips - 57
Hawkins didn't never play nothin' much by himself. I mean, only with Fletcher.
